items.summary: Disposition: evidence_needed for fleet-wide security clearance; blocked for public exposure and security-sensitive releases; conditional for ordinary reversible growth. Evidence: fleet-doctor has no run or control results; operations deploy-health, uptime, and error sweeps have no results; authentication and access boundaries, secrets handling, runtime isolation, release approvals and provenance, dependency and supply-chain controls, data exposure, monitoring, incident response, complete TLS posture, and security.txt/disclosure readiness remain unverified. No certificates are reported expiring within 30 days, but this does not prove complete TLS coverage. Compliance is a technical baseline only: 37 pass, 15 fail, and 7 unknown, with banner, consent, analytics, privacy, and terms findings open. Retained worker and reviewer failures are containment signals, not proof of exploitation. Exact decision: preserve private launch gates; allow only bounded reversible growth that adds no credentials, permissions, dependencies, new data collection, or cross-site behavior and preserves existing consent, disclosure, data-handling, and claims boundaries. Continue the existing read-only evidence matrix; do not create new production work, requeue, deploy, access credentials, modify permissions, add dependencies, or conduct external outreach.

Retain the existing bounded read-only security evidence matrix. Record dated, redacted evidence, affected scope, owners, explicit unknowns, severity, and release implications for authentication and access boundaries, secrets exposure, runtime isolation, release and deployment controls, dependency provenance, TLS, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and disclosure readiness. Do not create duplicate requests or production work.
